Here is the complete CLI sequence to enter configuration mode, apply all requested changes (including Cisco best-practice interface hardening), exit back to privileged EXEC, and save the configuration:

```
configure terminal
interface GigabitEthernet0/1
  description [WAN]-[CCT12345]-[100/1000]
  no shutdown
  ip address 192.168.0.1/24
  storm-control broadcast level 10
  udld aggressive
  no ip redirects
end
write memory
```

**Explanation of each step:**
- `configure terminal` – enters global configuration mode
- `interface GigabitEthernet0/1` – navigates to the target interface
- `description [WAN]-[CCT12345]-[100/1000]` – sets the exact interface description
- `no shutdown` – sets the interface to administratively up
- `ip address 192.168.0.1/24` – applies the required IP address and subnet mask
- `storm-control broadcast level 10` – limits broadcast traffic (CIS best-practice hardening)
- `udld aggressive` – enables aggressive UniDirectional Link Detection (hardening)
- `no ip redirects` – suppresses ICMP redirect messages on the point-to-point WAN link (hardening)
- `end` – exits directly to privileged EXEC (`#`) mode
- `write memory` – saves the running configuration to the startup configuration in NVRAM

exit
exit

* `ip address 192.168.0.1 255.255.255.0` = 192.168.0.1/24
* Hardening applied: description, no IP redirects, no proxy-ARP, no directed broadcast, CDP disabled on a WAN edge. `copy running-config startup-config` or `write memory` saves the config to NVRAM.
